title: Where an image comes from
subtitle: The caches a product photo passes on its way to your screen

scenes.title: Fetching a product photo
scenes.narration: When your browser needs a product photo, it asks a stack of places in order, nearest first. Here is a first visit, when none of them has the photo yet.

steps.say: The browser looks in its memory first. Nothing there on a first visit.
Then in its disk cache. Not there either.
So the request goes to the nearest edge server of the CDN. On a busy shop, this is where nearly every photo is found.
This time the edge does not have it, so it asks our own servers, which read the original from storage and shrink it.
On the way back up, the edge keeps a copy for a week.
And the browser keeps one too, so the next time this photo shows at once.

scenes.title: Where a day's photo requests were answered
scenes.narration: Over one day, here is where the photos were actually found.

steps.say: Most come straight from the browser's own cache.
Only two in a hundred reach our servers at all.
